correctness.rationale: GP(10,2) is specified by its 30 edges; exhaustive independent union-find and traversal cycle predicates agree on all 1,048,576 masks and return 755,608 simplices. The explicitly described vertex-toggle matching contains 377,742 pairs and 124 critical nonempty faces, all in dimensions 11 and 12 (34 and 90). A directed Hasse topological sort exhausts 755,608 vertices/6,967,280 incidences, proving acyclicity. The signed integral 34-by-90 Morse differential is computed via exact gradient recurrences; its 125 nonzero entries are all ±1. A fully integral unimodular row/column elimination isolates 24 unit pivots and zero residual, giving homology Z^10 in degree 11 and Z^66 in degree 12 without torsion. Since the Morse CW model has cells only in those two adjacent dimensions above 2, attaching maps are determined by the degree matrix, and the unit cancellations prove the asserted integral sphere-wedge homotopy equivalence. The actual embedded verify.cpp was compiled and executed; the complete source reconstructs every certificate without external datasets. No asymptotic claim or uncertified infinite inference is made.

originality.rationale: Full accessible scientific text of Taylan (2015) establishes devoid-complex and matching-tree frameworks but not this forbidden-all-cycles homotopy calculation on GP(10,2). Zuffi (2017) explicitly defines the same induced-acyclic-vertex complex but contains no dodecahedral classification. Carnero Bravo (2023) explicitly studies the induced-forest vertex complex but its inspected graph-family theorems concern paths, cycles, cactus, multipartite and certain product graphs, not the 20-vertex dodecahedral graph nor a theorem subsuming it. Semantic published-finding corpus searches of the exact assertion, notation aliases, both Betti numbers, generalized Petersen family and stronger possible classifications surfaced dodecahedral independence/matching/graph-configuration/Rips computations, none involving the vertex-induced cycle-free complex. This is best-knowledge originality; neither division of assignments nor failed searching is treated as proof of absolute uniqueness.

value.rationale: The natural invariant is the simplicial complex of vertex-induced forests of the canonical planar cubic dodecahedral graph, explicitly motivated by forest filtrations and feedback vertex sets. Its 755,608 faces do not reveal whether the homotopy is a single sphere wedge, mixed-dimensional, or torsion-bearing. The exact integral answer is a mixed bouquet of ten 11-spheres and sixty-six 12-spheres and is certified by an acyclic Morse matching and a fully unimodular 24-pivot boundary. This is a complete, reproducible topological classification for a natural, symmetric, highly cyclic graph, not a restatement of a published independence or matching table, a small normalization exercise, or a speculative generalization. No downstream general theorem is claimed.
